findings.message: All three performance/reliability gate thresholds in §5 are expressed solely as @threshold registry tags (PRD.01.perf.redirectp95, PRD.01.perf.screeningdeadline, PRD.01.reliability.countstaleness) with no concrete numeral anywhere in the TDD. Cases TDD.01.04.1a5d and TDD.01.04.2b6e assert threshold conditions without providing the millisecond values an implementer can code an assertion against. The @threshold deferral is acceptable as a named reference, but the TDD must also state the default/fallback concrete value (or explicitly note that the threshold file must be present for the test suite to run).
findings.recommendation: For each @threshold tag in §5 and each affected case, add a parenthetical concrete bound derived from PRD-01 (e.g., 'PRD.01.perf.redirectp95 = 200 ms per PRD-01 §X'). If PRD-01 has not yet resolved these, add a TDD-level assumption table in §5 that states the assumed values under which the performance gate is verified and note these as pending PRD confirmation. Cases TDD.01.04.1a5d and TDD.01.04.2b6e must carry an inline numeric timeout assertion seed so they are runnable from day one.

findings.message: The overload-shed load tests (resolve read-load 1a5d, create-load 2b6e) assert 'beyond a safe-overload margin the path fast-fails and sheds', but the safe-overload margin is named only qualitatively — no concrete multiplier or absolute rate is defined. A test asserting 'sheds beyond the margin' with no defined margin is a tautology: any shed point passes, including one that sheds at design load (false-negative on capacity regression) or one that never sheds before pool exhaustion.
findings.recommendation: Quantify the safe-overload margin in SPEC §6 as a concrete factor of design load (e.g., shed engages at >= K x sustained rate) and have 1a5d/2b6e assert the bounded degraded/shed response at exactly that K, plus a paired assertion that p95 still holds AT design load (margin lower edge). Without the literal number these two type:performance cases cannot satisfy C2.

findings.message: Audit-emission tests for the read_counts deny path (f82b) and mark_taken_down takedown/re-mark (093c) assert only that an audit event is emitted, not the full field set. SPEC §5 'Audit events' requires every event carry {subject, action, resource, decision, timestamp, reason}; only the read_original_url test (e71a) asserts that field set. A test that checks emission but not field completeness passes even if the deny/takedown event omits subject, decision, or reason — defeating the traceability the SPEC names.
findings.recommendation: Promote f82b and 093c to type: security and assert the full {subject, action, resource, decision, timestamp, reason} field set on their audit events, matching e71a. For 093c, assert the takedown event identifies the acting subject and decision so an unauthorized takedown of a live code is attributable.

findings.location: §4 increment_visit (TDD.01.04.3c6f / 4d70 / d609); SPEC §3 delivery contract, DFD Count path
findings.message: The increment_visit operation crosses a trust boundary (SPEC DFD 'Count path': code + event_id arriving off a durable async dispatch queue) but has no input-fuzzing test. d609 covers only producer/consumer version-skew; 4d8f and 81c3 fuzz put_mapping URL and resolve/mark_taken_down ShortCode, but neither covers the event payload. A malformed/oversized/encoding-edge/injection event_id or code decoded from the transport is an un-fuzzed boundary input — the deserialization surface flagged by ADR-01's threat model is only tested for version skew, not for hostile payload content.
findings.recommendation: Add a type: security (CWE-20) fuzzing case on increment_visit: malformed/oversized/encoding-edge/injection event_id and code (and any decoded event field) are rejected to dead-letter before mutating VisitCountRecord, never best-effort decoded. Also fuzz put_mapping's ShortCode parameter (currently only resolve/mark_taken_down ShortCode is fuzzed by 81c3, though §5 names the allowlist as a precondition on put_mapping too).

findings.message: Three unit test cases appear in §4 but have no corresponding row in the §3 mapping table: TDD.01.04.2b4d (put_mapping idempotent same-(code,url) retry), TDD.01.04.5e90 (resolve of a known ACTIVE code), and TDD.01.04.f83a (mark_taken_down of a never-issued code -> UnknownCodeError). The §3 table — which is the traceability manifest — does not list them, so the coverage count of '35 cases' in §3 and the header 'files (test-first)' is inconsistent with the §4 body. Note: the auditor accepted these as legitimate SPEC-contract-completeness cases; this P3 surfaces the traceability-visibility gap only, not a substantive error.
findings.recommendation: Add a @spec: SPEC-01 §3 row to the §3 mapping table for each of the three orphan cases, citing the interface docstring clause each validates: TDD.01.04.2b4d traces to the 'identical (code,url) retry is idempotent' clause; TDD.01.04.5e90 traces to the basic resolve happy-path; TDD.01.04.f83a traces to the UnknownCodeError clause of mark_taken_down. Update the §3 coverage summary row and case count accordingly.

findings.message: TDD.01.04.e71a bundles the permit path and the deny path for read_original_url into a single integration case ('permit + deny verified together'). Combining two distinct outcomes in one case means a failure signal names the combined case rather than the failing path, reducing diagnostic precision. If the permit path regresses, the deny-path assertion also runs in the same case body, potentially masking the specific failure branch.
findings.recommendation: Split TDD.01.04.e71a into two sibling cases: one for the permit path (role translation + grant evaluation + audit event emitted) and one for the deny path (same role translation, no grant, AccessDenied raised, audit event emitted, no value disclosed). The DB-role translation assertion can be factored into a shared fixture or helper used by both.

findings.message: Standby-loss durability halt (ADR.01.05.5896): 81b4 asserts DurabilityHaltError fail-closed (failure detected) and states 'the retry is retryable on standby recovery using bounded backoff' — but this is a property claim about retryability, not an executed recovery assertion. The test does not appear to restore the standby and assert put_mapping subsequently succeeds idempotently. The impl could stay permanently halted (never re-admitting writes after standby returns) undetected.
findings.recommendation: Extend 81b4 (or add a paired e2e) to: inject standby loss -> assert DurabilityHaltError -> restore standby -> assert the retried identical put_mapping succeeds and the durability-halt signal clears. Mirror the degrade->recover pattern already present in 4d80.

findings.message: SPEC §6 explicitly calls out 'bounded exponential backoff with jitter so a synchronized retry does not storm the recovering standby'. 81b4 asserts 'bounded backoff with jitter (no storm)' as a property of a single retry, but does not exercise the actual cascade: many DurabilityHalt'd writers retrying concurrently the moment the standby recovers. An impl with backoff-without-jitter (or insufficient jitter) would pass 81b4 as written while still storming the recovering standby in production.
findings.recommendation: Add an integration case that halts N concurrent writers on standby loss, restores the standby, and asserts the retry arrival distribution is spread (no synchronized thundering herd) and the standby is not re-saturated on recovery — turning the jitter claim into an exercised assertion.

findings.message: Rollback path for ADR-named one-way decisions is not exercised at TDD layer. The two one-way decisions (synchronous commit-before-ack, declarative unique constraint) have behavioral smoke coverage but no test validates the deployment rollback path — i.e., that the schema migration introducing the unique constraint can be rolled back non-destructively, or that the replication-mode configuration can be reverted. This gap is appropriately deferred to the IPLAN/DPLAN layer.
findings.recommendation: Record an explicit IPLAN-layer action item for the declarative-constraint migration rollback: (1) verify the constraint drop is non-destructive on a non-prod copy before promoting to prod; (2) verify synchronous_commit can be reverted without dropping committed rows. Reference this TDD in the rollback runbook so the ADR traceability is maintained.

findings.message: The mapping_store_degraded counter is labelled by degradation_type in both SPEC §6 and case a3d6, but neither document enumerates the allowed values of that label. If degradation_type is derived from raw exception class names, network error strings, or any other unbounded source, the label cardinality is unbounded and will cause metric series explosion in any time-series backend with high-cardinality label costs (Prometheus, Datadog, etc.).
findings.recommendation: Enumerate the allowed degradation_type label values in SPEC §6 (e.g., unreachable, dns, tls, timeout) and enforce in the implementation that only those values are emitted. Add a TDD assertion to case a3d6 that the emitted degradation_type value is a member of the declared allowlist.
